content:
We need to build complete retrosynthesis route JSON. Inputs: we have three template searches and apply_template results giving precursors.

We need to construct route for target molecule? Not explicitly given. Likely the target is the molecule from template_search-1 mapping? The mapped_rxn shows product SMILES: "[CH3:1][O:2][c:3]1...". That's the target molecule. So route: root mol with that SMILES, then reaction using template_id 1914393, children are two precursor molecules from apply_template-1: "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1" and "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1". Then each of those may be further broken? Possibly need to apply other templates? The other two templates maybe for those precursors? Let's see: template 1914394 applied to some molecule (maybe the second precursor?). The apply_template-2 gave precursors ["FC1CN(Cc2ccc(cc2))C1","ClCCl"] for template 1914394. That seems similar to second precursor but with CCl? The second precursor from first reaction is "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1". That contains a CCl aromatic substituent. The template 1914394 seems to break a CCl to ClCCl? Actually mapping: product includes "FC1CN(... )C1". So applying template 1914394 to that product yields precursors: "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(cc2))C1" (removing CCl) and "ClCCl" (source of CCl). So we can further decompose second precursor.

Similarly template 1914395 applied to something yields precursor "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". That seems like maybe first precursor? The first precursor "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1" is a phenoxy with amide etc. Not matching. The third template maybe applies to something else? The precursor "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1" is similar to "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1" but with O instead of F and no CCl. Not sure.

We might need to build a 3-level route: target -> reaction1 (template1914393) -> two precursors A and B. Then B -> reaction2 (template1914394) -> precursors B1 and B2. Then maybe B1 -> reaction3 (template1914395) -> precursor C? Actually apply_template-3 gave precursor "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". That could be from applying template1914395 to something (maybe B1?). The mapped_rxn for template1914395 shows product with F substituent, reactant with O? Wait mapped_rxn: O[CH:2]1...>>[F:1][CH:2]1... So forward reaction replaces O with F. So reverse (retrosynthesis) replaces F with O. So applying template1914395 to product with F gives precursor with O. So B (which has F) could be turned into O version. Indeed B is "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1". Applying template1914395 to that would give "OC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1". But apply_template-3 gave "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1" (no CCl). So maybe they applied to a different molecule.

Given limited info, maybe we just need to construct route using the given data: root molecule (target) -> reaction using template1914393 -> children mols as given. Then for each child, if there is a further reaction data, include. We have for second child (FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1) we have a reaction using template1914394 producing two precursors. For the first child, we have no further data. Also we have a reaction using template1914395 producing precursor "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". Not sure where to attach.

Maybe the third reaction is applied to the first precursor after deprotecting? The first precursor "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1" contains a methoxy (CO) group. Template1914395 seems to replace F with O, not relevant.

Thus likely route: target -> reaction1914393 -> two precursors A and B. Then B -> reaction1914394 -> B1 and B2. Then B1 -> reaction1914395 -> C. That matches: B1 is "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(cc2))C1" (no CCl). Applying template1914395 to that yields "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". Yes B1 matches: "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(cc2))C1" (no CCl). Apply template1914395 (replace F with O) gives "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1". That matches apply_template-3 output. Good.

So route: root mol (target SMILES from mapped_rxn product). Reaction node template1914393 with children mol A and mol B. Then for mol B, reaction node template1914394 with children mol B1 and mol B2 (ClCCl). Then for mol B1, reaction node template1914395 with child mol C (OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1). No further.

We need target SMILES: from template_search-1 mapped_rxn product side: after ">>". The product SMILES is "[CH3:1][O:2][c:3]1...". That's the target. Provide as is.

Thus construct JSON.

Let's assemble.

Root:
{
"type":"mol",
"smiles":"[CH3:1][O:2][c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][c:7]([NH:8][C:9](=[O:10])[c:11]2[n:12][n:13][n:14]([CH2:15][c:16]3[cH:17][cH:18][c:19]([CH2:20][N:21]4[CH2:22][CH:23]([F:24])[CH2:25]4)[cH:26][cH:27]3)[c:28]2[NH2:29])[cH:30]1"
,
"children":[
{
"type":"reaction",
"template_id":1914393,
"children":[
{"type":"mol","smiles":"COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1"},
{"type":"mol","smiles":"FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1"}
]
}
]
}

Now need to add further children under second mol? The schema expects each mol can have children? Typically route is tree where reaction nodes are children of mol nodes. So we need to embed reaction under the second mol node. So modify: second mol node will have its own children array containing reaction node.

Thus root children: two mol nodes? Actually typical format: mol node has children reactions. In example, root mol has children array containing reaction node. Reaction node children are mols (precursors). Those precursor mol nodes could have their own children (reactions). So we need to embed further.

Thus root mol children: one reaction node (template1914393). That reaction node children: mol A and mol B. For mol B, we need to add its children: a reaction node template1914394. So mol B object will have "children": [ {reaction...} ].

Similarly mol B1 will have reaction1914395.

Let's construct.

Mol A: no further.

Mol B: smiles "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1", children: reaction1914394.

Reaction1914394 children: mol B1 "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(cc2))C1" and mol B2 "ClCCl".

Mol B1: children reaction1914395.

Reaction1914395 children: mol C "OC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1".

Mol B2: leaf.

Mol C: leaf.

Now produce JSON.
